newsitem.title: USA: North America bunkers mostly lower, supply strong.
newsitem.headline: North America bunkers mostly lower, supply strong.

text.p: North American bunker prices mostly fell in moderate trade this week amid tough competition among suppliers on the East Coast and selling off on the West Coast, players said on Tuesday.
The decline in NYMEX December crude oil futures, which have fallen to $22.64 a barrel, also helped push the market lower, traders said.
"Everyone's competing in New York and Philadelphia. Most of the majors are out here with supply," said one East Coast trader.
In the East Coast, New York Harbor spot 380 CST fell $4 from last Thursday, trading between $113 and $114 a tonne. The product dropped $9 last week.
Harbor 180 CST dropped $8 to $116/117 but diesel remained stable at $220/225.
In the Gulf Coast, Houston spot 380 CST fell $5 to $107/108 and 180 CST dropped $6 to 110/111 amid a selloff of supply at what traders said were cheap values.
The West Coast was slightly higher, but values were above much of the rest of world and so were expected to come down.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk + 1 212 859-1631
